newsitem.title: UK: Kvaerner wins $30 mln China contract.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner wins $30 mln China contract.

text.p: Kvaerner John Brown said on Wednesday it had won a $30 million contract to build a new plant in China.

"The contract...was awarded by the Jilin Chemical Industrial Corporation (JCIC)...It will enable JCIC to upgrade and expand its existing oxo plant at Jilin City which currently produces approximately 70,000 metric tons of oxo alcohols," the firm said in a statement.

Kvaerner John Brown, part of Norwegian industrial group Kvaerner ASA, said its Portsmouth office in the south of England would "undertake the engineering and procurement and provide technical assistance in China".

The contract will cover "a new oxo synthesis plant for converting propylene to 140,000 metric tons per year of butraldehydes" and "a 70,000 metric tons per year alcohols plant in which JCIC will produce butanol or 2-ethylhexanol".
Oxo alcohols are chemical plasticisers, ingredients added to plastics to make them more malleable and flexible.
